claims.text: A single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti high-entropy alloy has suppressed orbital moments and coercivity below 15 Oe.
The initial single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy has a magnetic ordering temperature above room temperature.
Intermediate-temperature annealing near 600 °C can induce hierarchical phase decomposition.
The proposed processing will form coherent nanoscale BCC precipitates enriched in Ti and/or Cr within an fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix.
The secondary Cr-rich or Ti-rich BCC phase will be antiferromagnetic.
Coherent fcc/BCC interfaces will act as magnetic domain-wall pinning sites.
Exchange coupling to the antiferromagnetic secondary phase will produce exchange bias or modify the local magnetic anisotropy of the adjacent fcc matrix.
Positive mixing enthalpies analogous to those of Fe-Cr or Al-Cr systems will drive formation of the secondary BCC phase.
The antiferromagnetic secondary phase will locally suppress net magnetization while increasing interfacial magnetic anisotropy through exchange coupling.
Hierarchical decomposition in the cited Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloy is associated with an increase in coercivity from 4.3 Oe to 39.4 Oe.
Interfacial exchange coupling and physical domain-wall pinning will overcome orbital-moment suppression in the single-phase fcc system.
The dual-phase fcc/BCC Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy will have coercivity exceeding 100 Oe.
The dual-phase alloy will have lower saturation magnetization than its single-phase counterpart.
The dual-phase alloy will retain a Curie temperature well above 300 K.
The resulting BCC precipitates will be 3–100 nm in size.
Coercivity enhancement requires the secondary phase to remain coherent and nanoscale.
Growth of the secondary phase beyond 1 μm or loss of interface coherence will reduce pinning efficiency and may return coercivity to baseline.
Thermal coarsening or decomposition of the secondary phase at operating temperature will degrade coercivity.
The coercivity increase depends on lattice mismatch and exchange-coupling strength at the fcc/BCC interface.
The cited records do not directly test the role of Ti in an fcc Fe-Co-Ni matrix.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the hypothesis applies only when precipitates are coherent, but the falsification rule says that observing incoherent or amorphous precipitates with low coercivity invalidates the coherent-interface mechanism. A sample outside the stated applicability boundary cannot decisively falsify that mechanism.
The operating range is described as significantly above room temperature but is given as 300–600 K; 300 K is approximately room temperature rather than significantly above it.

The design gives the homogeneous control and precipitate-bearing sample different heat treatments, while the rule refers to comparison under identical processing conditions. Processing differences could confound attribution to phase constitution.
